conclusions.rationale: List contents, CRUD with confirmation, quantified validation (1-60 trimmed name, case-insensitive uniqueness, 1-8000 text, max 50 prompts) and restart persistence are testable.

source_citations.excerpt: A prompt is valid when its trimmed name has 1–60 characters and is unique case-insensitively, and its text has 1–8000 characters. The library holds at most 50 prompts.
Persist a validated prompt library with stable ids, names, texts, optional provider/model override and 0–2 shortcuts

conclusions.rationale: Upgrade rules are explicit: existing prompts and selection unchanged, six named starters added once when absent by name and only under the limit, invalid legacy prompts kept but flagged and unusable until edited. SC-003 measures the preservation.

source_citations.excerpt: the starter prompts Minimal correction, Friendly rephrasing, Clarify, Shorten, Notes and Translate to English are added once when absent by name
Existing prompts that break the new validation rules are kept, flagged invalid and cannot be used until edited.

conclusions.rationale: Switch semantics, trigger-to-prompt mapping, per-dictation indicator choice without default change, and a quantified menu budget (200 ms, no focus theft) are testable. Under the constitution, the Windows/Linux part of 'every platform where the indicator is shown' is pending release evidence, which does not block implementation.

source_citations.excerpt: The plain dictation shortcut starts with "None", the post-processing shortcut with the default prompt, and a prompt shortcut with its prompt.
The menu opens within 200 ms without taking keyboard focus from the user's application, on every platform where the indicator is shown.
without changing the default

conclusions.rationale: Default vs override resolution, the existing provider set and not-ready reporting with the missing item are specific; processing with a not-ready provider skips the AI step, which AC-005 then treats as a failure with fallback.

source_citations.excerpt: A prompt whose provider lacks a required endpoint, model or API key is shown as not ready with the missing item; processing with it skips the AI step.
report provider readiness

conclusions.rationale: The 2026-10-14 decision makes the notice truthful: the indicator states for at least 4 seconds that the AI step failed and that the original text was used for insertion, and never claims insertion success, which belongs to 006/007/010. This removes the round-1 contradiction that made the criterion unreachable when insertion cannot be verified. Failure classes, the 30 s whole-step bound, history content and cancellation behavior are testable. Residual 'inserted' wording elsewhere (Timeout scenario, FR-004) describes the insertion attempt, not the notice text, and is recorded as a warning finding.

source_citations.excerpt: the indicator states for at least 4 seconds that the AI step failed and that the original text was used for insertion (it never states that the insertion succeeded: the insertion result is reported by 006, 007 and 010)
Cancelling during processing inserts nothing; history behaves as today for cancelled dictations.
It never states that the insertion succeeded: the insertion result (attempted, verified, failed, recovery) belongs to 006, 007 and 010 and is reported by them.

conclusions.rationale: 0-2 shortcuts per prompt, activation-mode behavior, conflict checking via 004's shared checker and shortcut removal on confirmed delete are testable once 004's checker exists; the dependency on 004 is declared in Clarifications.

source_citations.excerpt: Prompt shortcuts use the shared conflict checker of feature 004 against every other shortcut.
Deleting a prompt removes its shortcuts after confirmation.

conclusions.rationale: Test panel inputs, outputs, 30 s limit and the no-insert/no-history guarantees are observable; FR-005 restates the guarantee.

source_citations.excerpt: A test never inserts text into another application and never writes history.
Provide a test operation that never inserts text or writes history.

conclusions.rationale: The CLI operation set, delegation of prompt shortcuts to 004's shortcut operations, key redaction in stdout/stderr/logs, readiness reporting and the JSON envelope with stable codes are explicit; SC-002 gives the measurable secret-scan.

source_citations.excerpt: The settings CLI (008) offers prompt list, create, update, delete, set-default and set-provider-override (provider id and model, or `--clear` to return to the default provider)
Outputs never contain API keys, in stdout, stderr or logs
without ever outputting API keys

conclusions.rationale: Library persistence with stable ids, override and shortcuts, plus once-only migration/starters; detailed by AC-001/AC-002/AC-006.

source_citations.excerpt: migrate existing prompts and add starter prompts once

conclusions.rationale: Per-dictation prompt resolution from trigger and indicator choice without changing the default; Story 2 mermaid and AC-003 define the mapping.

source_citations.excerpt: Resolve the prompt of each dictation from its trigger (plain, post-processing or prompt shortcut) and from a per-dictation choice made on the indicator, without changing the default.

conclusions.rationale: Resolved provider/model, readiness reporting and a 30 s bound including retries and fallbacks are measurable.

source_citations.excerpt: bound the whole step, including internal retries and fallback requests, to 30 seconds

conclusions.rationale: Fallback to the initial transcript with failure recording and cancellation respect; 'Insert' here means the insertion attempt via the output pipeline. Consistent with the reworded AC-005 once read that way (see warning finding).

source_citations.excerpt: Insert the initial transcript and record the failure whenever the AI step does not produce a valid result; respect cancellation.
Provide a test operation that never inserts text or writes history.

conclusions.rationale: CLI read/modify including override set/clear, without key output.

source_citations.excerpt: Expose prompt read and modify operations, including setting and clearing the per-prompt provider/model override, through the settings CLI without ever outputting API keys.

conclusions.rationale: Fault-injection with five enumerated failure classes and a 100% target is measurable at the processing boundary (initial transcript handed to insertion and failure recorded).

source_citations.excerpt: In fault-injection tests (provider error, HTTP error, timeout of the whole step, empty result, not ready), 100% of dictations insert the initial transcript and record the failure.

conclusions.rationale: Zero key occurrences across CLI outputs and logs is a binary, automatable check.

source_citations.excerpt: Secret scanning of CLI outputs and logs across all prompt operations finds zero API key occurrences.

conclusions.rationale: Upgrade fixture comparison of prompts, texts and selection is deterministic.

source_citations.excerpt: Upgrading a store with custom prompts keeps all prompts, texts and the selected prompt unchanged.

ambiguities.question: When the overlay style is none (indicator hidden), where is the at-least-4-second AI failure notice shown?

citations.excerpt: the indicator states for at least 4 seconds that the AI step failed
The indicator is hidden (overlay style none): prompt choice is available only through shortcuts and settings.

findings.description: After the AC-005 rewording, several statements still say the initial transcript 'is inserted' (Timeout scenario, Story 4 flowchart, FR-004, SC-001, Edge Cases). They read as the insertion attempt through the output pipeline, but a tester could take them as a claim of verified insertion, which the 2026-10-14 decision assigns to 006/007/010.
findings.suggestion: On the next spec-refine, align these sentences on 'used for insertion' or 'handed to insertion'.

citations.excerpt: Then processing is abandoned and the initial transcript is inserted
Insert the initial transcript and record the failure
on timeout the initial transcript is inserted

findings.description: AC-006 and the prompt-shortcut part of AC-008 rely on feature 004 (shared conflict checker and shortcut operations); they cannot be delivered before 004.
findings.suggestion: Keep 004 as a declared prerequisite of the shortcut steps in the plan.

citations.excerpt: Prompt shortcuts use the shared conflict checker of feature 004 against every other shortcut.
prompt shortcuts are managed with the shortcut operations of feature 004

findings.description: prompt-settings and recording-indicator mockups, semantic and test IDs are deferred to the program-wide Penflow pass before spec-ship; UI visual states cannot be certified until then.
findings.suggestion: Gate the UI step of the plan on that Penflow pass.
